title: Indexes
summary: Understand what indexes do and write single, compound, unique, text and hashed indexes.

quiz.q: What is the main benefit of an index?
options: It makes the stored data smaller
It lets MongoDB find matching documents without reading the whole collection
It stops other users from reading the data
It checks that every field has the right type
quiz.explain: An index is a sorted lookup structure. It speeds up reads, but it uses extra storage and slows writes a little.

quiz.q: Complete the call to create an ascending index on `marks`.
quiz.explain: `1` is ascending order and `-1` is descending.

quiz.q: You have an index `{ customerId: 1, createdAt: -1 }`. Which query can use it well?
options: None, compound indexes only work with all fields
quiz.explain: A compound index serves queries that start with its first field (`customerId`), alone or together with the next. A query on only the second field cannot use it well.

quiz.q: What does `db.users.createIndex({ email: 1 }, { unique: true })` do?
options: It deletes users with the same email
It makes the database refuse a second user with an email that already exists
It sorts the users by email permanently
quiz.explain: A unique index rejects duplicates. The insert or update that would create the duplicate fails with an error.

quiz.q: Which statements about text and hashed indexes are true? Choose two.
options: A collection may have only one text index
A hashed index is ideal for range queries like marks above 80
A hashed index supports equality matches only
A text index is created with { name: -1 }
quiz.explain: Text indexes are limited to one per collection and are created with the value 'text'. Hashed values cannot be ordered, so ranges are not supported.

exercise.task:
Write four index commands in `indexes.js`:

- A **unique** index on `email` in the `users` collection.
- A **compound** index on `orders`: `customerId` ascending, then `createdAt` descending.
- A **text** index on `description` in the `products` collection.
- A **hashed** index on `userId` in the `sessions` collection.
hints: Each command has the form `db.<collection>.createIndex(<fields>, <options>)`. Only the unique one needs the options object.
The unique one ends with `{ unique: true }`. Use `'text'` and `'hashed'` as the value instead of 1 for the last two. Use `1` and `-1` for the compound one.

db.users.createIndex({ email: 1 }, { unique: true })
db.orders.createIndex({ customerId: 1, createdAt: -1 })
db.products.createIndex({ description: 'text' })
db.sessions.createIndex({ userId: 'hashed' })

checks.name: A compound index on orders: customerId 1, createdAt -1
checks.hint: List both fields in one object, in this order: { customerId: 1, createdAt: -1 }.

checks.name: A text index on products.description
checks.hint: Use the string 'text' as the value: { description: 'text' }.

checks.name: A hashed index on sessions.userId
checks.hint: Use the string 'hashed' as the value: { userId: 'hashed' }.
